findings.title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors
findings.body: The new logging in CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags uses Error unconditionally, including when fetching and deleting succeed and when the final batch is empty. Normal cleanup therefore produces error-level messages even when nothing is wrong, triggering false failure alerts and logging entire ID batches at normal production verbosity. These messages should be removed or logged at debug level, reserving Error for actual failures.

findings.title: The shorter ticker increases load for every cleanup job
findings.body: Changing the ticker from ten minutes to one minute accelerates all cleanup jobs, including dashboard-version deletion, snapshot deletion, filesystem cleanup, and query-history maintenance—not just annotations. This can run their database queries and filesystem scans up to ten times as often. Since a cleanup pass may run for nine minutes, passes lasting over one minute will also have a tick queued and can restart immediately, keeping maintenance continuously active. Preserve the existing cadence or isolate any intended annotation scheduling change.

findings.title: SQLite ID-list construction has quadratic allocation cost
findings.body: In deleteByIDs, each iteration formats the entire accumulated SQLite ID list into a new string. Building a batch of n IDs therefore copies and allocates O(n²) bytes. At the newly tested batch size of 32,767, this entails several gigabytes of cumulative copying and allocation to produce a DELETE statement only a few hundred kilobytes long, adding substantial CPU and garbage-collection overhead to cleanup. Build the list with a strings.Builder or an append-based buffer instead.

findings.title: Parameterized deletes exceed PostgreSQL's bind-parameter limit
findings.body: deleteByIDs now creates one bind parameter per selected ID on PostgreSQL, which supports at most 65,535 parameters in a statement. With a configured AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize above that limit and enough eligible rows, the DELETE fails and cleanup repeatedly aborts without removing that batch. The previous subquery-based DELETE did not impose this parameter limit. Bound each DELETE to the dialect's parameter limit or split the selected IDs into smaller deletes.
